content: Always provide live, verifiable evidence when a technical customer asks about performance metrics; avoid vague claims.
Use assumptive close after demonstrating value and summarizing pain points; it works well when the customer has shown clear buying signals.
Maintain language consistency: do not mix languages in responses, especially when quoting technical data.
In in-store scenarios, prioritize hands-on demonstrations and real-time tests over verbal explanations.
When a customer asks for specific data (e.g., battery drain rate), provide a direct answer or offer to measure it live rather than repeating general specs.

name: Live Stress Test Trust Builder
condition: When a technical customer questions performance under load.
example: Customer asks about thermal throttling. Salesperson: 'Let me run a 30-minute stress test right now. I'll show you real-time CPU temps and brightness.'

name: Pain Point Summary Close
condition: After demonstrating value and receiving positive feedback.
example: Salesperson: 'So your main issue was [pain point]. We've just shown that [product] solves it. Let's proceed with the order.'

name: Real-Time Data Sharing
condition: When customer asks for specific metrics (battery, temperature).
example: Salesperson: 'Here's the battery monitor on screen. After 20 minutes of dual-app use, it's at 95%. That translates to about 10 hours.'

objection: How's the battery holding up with both apps running?
rebuttal_template: Great question. Let me show you the battery monitor right now. We've been running both apps for [X] minutes, and the battery level is at [Y]%. Based on this rate, you can expect [Z] hours of continuous use. Want me to keep it running while we talk?

objection: Any thermal throttling or screen dimming after an hour?
rebuttal_template: Let's test that right now. I'll start a 30-minute timer with both apps open, and we can monitor the CPU temperature and brightness together. If you see any drop, we'll address it. Deal?

objection: I'm not sure this can replace my laptop.
rebuttal_template: I understand. Let's do a side-by-side comparison with your laptop. Plug in your laptop, open the same code editor and terminal, and we'll see which one stays cooler and smoother. You can judge for yourself.
